absent: Full decode and operand fetch logic preceding the emulation tail, including flag and width establishment.
Internals of register cache handling, memory writeback, string pointer advance, count update, completion test, condition test, branch computation, register accessors, and cache flush hook.
Exact numeric encodings of emulation control flags, completion codes, and external emulation results.
Guest extended state swap implementation, trace payloads, and reload counter definition.
Numeric values of synthetic interrupt masks, vector limits, page enable bits, MSR identifiers, and exit codes.
APIC virtualization inhibit reason set, required mask, kick and request mechanics, and platform callbacks.
Reverse-map and TDP leaf removal algorithms, flush scope, slot iteration, and address space layout.
Timer index assignment, pending bitmap layout, and kick semantics.
Interrupt notifier registration and global interrupt mapping lifecycle.
Zero page lifetime, unmapped frame handling, and dirty tracking implementation.
Host versus guest authentication for synthetic register writes and version register semantics.

findings.text: Emulation context exposes operations to discard cached register values, to commit them back, and to decide whether direct guest physical addressing is usable for the current decoded instruction.

Instruction emulation tail performs destination writeback unless flagged no-write, restores saved destination kind for reuse, advances string source and destination pointers, handles repeated string accounting by reducing the count register and either restarting without updating the instruction pointer or finishing with a flag cleared, then maps internal completion codes to external outcomes with conditional register commit.

Repeated string restart is requested when iteration progress and pending input buffer state indicate more work remains, in which case cached memory reads are cleared and registers committed before restart.

Two-byte opcode handling treats cache control and prefetch and no-operation encodings as successful no-ops, routes control and debug register moves through accessor hooks, applies conditional move and branch and byte set based on condition evaluation against flags, and widens byte or word sources with zero or sign extension to operation width, with other values reported as non-emulatable.
Direct guest physical use is refused when a repeat prefix accompanies a string operation or when the decoded operation touches two memory operands, otherwise allowed.

Fault propagation validates that the pending exception number lies within the architected range and otherwise fails emulation while recording presence of an exception; intercepted and unhandleable completions map to distinct external results without register commit.
Guest floating point management provides load and put helpers that exchange host and guest extended state around guest execution with usage checks, tracing, and a reload statistic.
Load assumes state is currently not in use and leaves processor key protection state for separate restoration, while put assumes state is in use and records a reload event.

Fixed width vector aliases describe sixteen byte and thirty two byte SIMD values with views as pairs of sixty four bit halves or quadruples of thirty two bit lanes plus constructors and selectors for halves and individual lanes.
Sparse virtual CPU set sizing rounds the maximum virtual CPU count up by per-bank density, and the extended call limit is a fixed offset beyond the query capabilities identifier.

Synthetic interrupt source state is read atomically, masked sources report absence of a vector while unmasked sources expose low vector bits, and connection and automatic end-of-interrupt status are determined by scanning all sources for a matching vector with the respective property.

Vector bitmap maintenance ignores vectors below the first valid value, updates connected and automatic membership, and when global automatic behavior transitions between empty and non-empty while virtualized interrupt handling is enabled it takes the APIC virtualization update lock in write mode to adjust a usage count and set or clear the Hyper-V inhibit reason.
Translation from synthetic interrupt controller state to its owning virtual CPU goes through the containing per-vCPU Hyper-V record.
Mapping from virtual CPU to its synthetic interrupt state goes through the per-vCPU Hyper-V record.

APIC virtualization inhibit update must be called with the update lock held in write mode, ignores reasons not required by the platform, merges interrupt window request state, and on transitions between fully enabled and inhibited it requests updates on all CPUs before publishing the new mask and invalidates the default APIC page when becoming inhibited.
Guest physical to guest frame translation discards the page offset by shift.

Guest frame range invalidation takes the MMU lock in write mode, brackets work with invalidate start and end markers, records the range, removes reverse-map and two-dimensional paging leaf entries, and flushes remote translation buffers only when removals occurred.

Reverse-map range removal iterates all address spaces and only slots overlapping the requested interval, clamps to slot boundaries, skips empty intersections, and reports whether any flush is required; it does nothing when the instance has no reverse maps.
Two-dimensional paging leaf removal asserts write ownership of the MMU lock and visits every valid root with safe yielding.

Invalidate tracking nests with a counter, initializes the tracked interval to invalid on outermost entry, widens the stored interval to the minimal cover of concurrent requests because partial subtraction is unsupported, then on exit advances a sequence number with ordering before decrementing the counter and warns when no interval was recorded.
Inhibit bit manipulation validates at build time that the traced reason table matches the reason count, then sets or clears the requested bit and emits a change trace.

Synthetic interrupt configuration validates the vector against the minimum unless masked or host-initiated to permit zero initialization, stores the new value atomically, refreshes membership for both old and new vectors, and requests an input controller scan.

Lookup of a virtual CPU by virtual processor index rejects indices beyond the maximum, fast-paths direct slot match on index equality, otherwise scans all virtual CPUs for equality and returns absence when unmatched.

Virtual processor index resolves to the stored Hyper-V index when the per-vCPU structure exists and otherwise to the creation position; the lock-free accessor uses acquire ordering to pair with initialization release.
Retrieval of synthetic interrupt state by virtual processor index requires successful CPU lookup, present Hyper-V state, and an active flag observed with single-read semantics.

Acknowledgement of a synthetic interrupt source redrives enabled non-direct timers bound to that source that have messages waiting, then under source synchronization forwards acknowledgement to the mapped global interrupt number when one is assigned.
Synthetic interrupt exit reporting captures control and event and message page state plus the triggering register identifier into the per-vCPU Hyper-V exit area and raises an exit request.

Synthetic interrupt register writes reject accesses while inactive except host clearing, trace the attempt, handle control and version and event and message page registers with guest-triggered exits and conditional zeroing of newly enabled guest pages, fan out end-of-message to every source, delegate numbered sources to the source programmer, and reject unknown registers.
Timer pending marking records the timer index in the per-vCPU pending set, raises a timer service request, and optionally kicks the target CPU.
Global interrupt acknowledgement notification walks the source-synchronized notifier list and invokes callbacks whose registered number matches.
Guest memory helpers expose clearing a byte range to zeros and writing a page slice, internally resolving slots and host addresses and marking pages dirty.
Clearing iterates page-bounded segments advancing frame by frame from the starting offset until the length is consumed, using a shared zero page as source.
Segment sizing caps a transfer at the remainder of the current page.

Host address resolution fails for missing or invalid slots and for writes to read-only slots, optionally reports remaining page counts, and error addresses are recognized by comparison against the kernel direct map boundary.
Host page writes reject transfers crossing the page boundary, reject unmapped or read-only translations, propagate copy failures as faults, and only mark dirty on success.

Default interrupt controller base occupies one guest frame that is invalidated when virtualization becomes inhibited, and message completion processing covers the full sixteen-entry source array addressed by a contiguous register range.

Per-vCPU synthetic state observed includes control, version, event and message page addresses, active and page-zero suppression flags, an array of source registers plus vector and auto end-of-interrupt bitmaps and source-to-global mappings, with timers carrying pending, enable, direct and source-index configuration.
Empty or inverted zap intervals, overlapping slot miscalculation, missing invalidate range, negative nesting, and overlong host writes trigger warnings or bug checks rather than silent corruption.
